title: This Frog Freezes Solid and Its Heart Stops Every Winter
subject: wood frog

scenes.text: This frog's heart stops every winter, and it's fine.
The wood frog. When the cold hits, about two thirds of the water in its body turns to ice.
It stops breathing. Its heart stops beating. It looks completely dead.
The trick is sugar. Its liver floods its body with glucose, which works like antifreeze.
That keeps ice crystals from forming where they would do the most damage.
In spring it thaws, the heart restarts, and the frog hops off. Stopped heart. Still alive.

description:
A wood frog can have roughly two thirds of its body water turn to ice.
It stops breathing and its heart stops beating, while glucose acts like antifreeze. In spring it thaws and its organs return to normal.
Could you survive a winter like that?
first_comment: Wood frogs even live north of the Arctic Circle. Which animal would you least expect to survive being frozen?
